title: Maven: dependencies, build lifecycle, plugins and repository

videos.script: A Java program that uses only the JDK is easy to build. One javac, one java. {{javac}} Then it needs a library. Now you find the jar, download it, and put it on two command lines. And that library needs four more of its own. {{classpath}} Maven turns this around. You write one file that says what the project is and what it needs. {{pom}} Maven fetches the libraries, and the libraries they need, from a shared repository. Then it compiles, tests and packages, in the same order on every machine. {{lifecycle}} This lesson starts by setting up the machine for the whole course. A JDK, Maven, and a check that both answer. {{setup}} Then you build a small project by hand. You read every line of its file, and see where each downloaded jar ends up. {{project}} And you watch a build fail because it trusted Maven's defaults. That failure is why every version in this course is written down. {{pins}}
